src: APPSC Group-II 2019
s: On whose plea did Swami Sitaram end his hunger strike?
x:
Swami Sitaram actively campaigned for the formation of a separate Andhra State and undertook a hunger strike to press this demand. He eventually withdrew his fast at the request of Acharya Vinoba Bhave, who appealed to him to end the agitation through peaceful and constitutional means. Vinoba Bhave's intervention played a significant role in persuading Swami Sitaram to discontinue his fast. Although the demand for Andhra State continued, it was later Potti Sreeramulu's fast unto death that ultimately led to the formation of Andhra State on 1 October 1953. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Hunger Strike Withdrawn on Appeal of – Vinoba Bhave
• Leader – Swami Sitaram

src: APPSC Group-II 2019
s: When did Potti Sriramulu become Amarajeevi?
x:
Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu sacrificed his life on 15 December 1952 after undertaking a 58- day fast unto death demanding the formation of a separate Andhra State. His martyrdom triggered widespread protests across the Telugu-speaking regions, compelling the Government of India to announce the formation of Andhra State, which came into existence on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as its capital. Potti Sriramulu is remembered as "Amarajeevi" for his supreme sacrifice. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Amarajeevi – Potti Sriramulu
• Date of Martyrdom – 15 December 1952
• Andhra State Formed – 1 October 1953

src: APPSC Group-II Mains 2025
s: Andhra State was formed on
x:
Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 by separating the Telugu-speaking districts from the erstwhile Madras State. It became the first linguistic state to be created in independent India. The formation of Andhra State was the culmination of a long struggle for a separate Telugu-speaking province. The movement reached its peak after the fast unto death by Potti Sreeramulu, who sacrificed his life on 15 December 1952 demanding a separate Andhra State. His martyrdom led to widespread protests, compelling the Government of India to accept the demand. Kurnool became the capital of the newly formed Andhra State, while the High Court was established at Guntur. Later, on 1 November 1956, Andhra State was merged with the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State to form Andhra Pradesh under the States Reorganisation Act. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Andhra State – 1 October 1953
• First Linguistic State in Independent India
• Capital – Kurnool
• High Court – Guntur

src: APPSC Group-II Mains 2025
s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:

A. Formation of the Visalandra Mahasabha

B. Dhar Commission

C. Swami Sitaram's fast

D. Formation of States Re-organization Commission
x:
The demand for a separate Andhra State and later a Visalandhra gained momentum after Independence through a series of political developments. The Dhar Commission was appointed in 1948 to examine the question of linguistic provinces. It did not recommend the formation of states on a linguistic basis. In 1949, the Visalandra Mahasabha was formed to campaign for the unification of all Telugu-speaking areas into a single state. Swami Sitaram undertook his fast in 1951 demanding the formation of Andhra State, which further intensified the movement. The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was constituted in 1953 under the chairmanship of Justice Fazl Ali to examine the reorganisation of states on linguistic and administrative grounds. Its recommendations eventually led to the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956. Thus, the correct chronological order is: Dhar Commission → Visalandra Mahasabha → Swami Sitaram's Fast → States Reorganisation Commission Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Dhar Commission – 1948
• Visalandra Mahasabha – 1949
• Swami Sitaram's Fast – 1951
• States Reorganisation Commission – 1953
